overall: The AG found the Authority violated the Open Meeting Law by omitting the date and time of posting from its official website notice, and found no violation on the location, executive session, and other topic-specificity allegations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the November 8 notice lacked the date and time the notice was posted.
Complaint alleged the November 8 notice lacked the meeting location address.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Authority complied with the Open Meeting Law's requirements where the date, time and place of its November 8 meeting were posted on its website.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session purposes on the notice were insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Authority did not convene in executive session on November 8, we find no violation with respect to the sufficiency of the executive session topics listed on the notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged other topics on the notice did not provide the required specifics.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the seven remaining topics were sufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: Not a complaint allegation: AG sua sponte noted City website notices were not easily located and the City website should link to Authority notices.
allegations.key_passage: we note that notices posted to the City website, www.cambridgema.gov, were not easily located.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate).
remedy_passage: We order the Authority's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
